title: Targeting Technician
raw_text:
8-131A. Military Occupational Specialty 131A--Targeting Technician
(Effective 202410)
   a. Licensing/certification requirement. None.
   b. Prerequisites. DA Cir 601 series.
   c. MOS 131A. MOS 131A is an accession MOS. Enlisted feeder MOS are 11B, 11C, 19D, 19K
and any CMF 13 MOS.
   d. Associated SQI.
        (1) 0--No special qualifications.
        (2) 8--Instructor.
        (3) P--Parachutist.
        (4) T--Transition (personnel only).
        (5) Z--Research, Development, Test, and Evaluation Technician.
   e. Associated ASI. (Note: Refer to table 6-6 (Listing of universal ASI’s associated with all
MOS)).
        (1) 5A—Joint Air Tactical Operations.
        (2) L8 – Joint Operational Fires and Effects (in grades W2-W4 only; personnel and
positions). (Effective 202610)
   f. Qualifications.
        (1) WO1/CW2 must--
              (a) Have a physical demands rating of Moderate (Gold).
              (b) A minimum OPAT score of Standing Long Jump (LJ) – 0120 cm, Seated Power
Throw (PT) – 0350 cm, Strength Deadlift (SD) – 0120 lbs., and Interval Aerobic Run (IR) -0036
shuttles in Physical Demand Category in “Moderate” (Gold).
              (c) Complete the Targeting Technician Warrant Officer Basic Course.
              (d) Meet physical standards per AR 40-501, chapter 2.
              (e) Have 20/40 correctable vision per AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-13 and 5-17 and
meet hearing standards per AR 40-501, paragraphs 2-7 and 5-18.
              (f) Be a U.S. citizen.
              (g) Hold a security clearance of SECRET.
              (h) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI) (Effective 202310).
        (2) CW3 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications listed in paragraph f (1).
              (b) Complete both phases of the Targeting Technician Warrant Officer Advanced
Course as a CW2 or CW3.
              (c) Possess a security eligibility of TOP SECRET with eligibility for access to
sensitive compartmented information (SCI).
        (3) CW4 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (2).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Intermediate Level Education (WOILE) as a CW3 or
CW4.
        (4) CW5 must--
              (a) Meet qualifications described in paragraph f (3).
              (b) Complete the Warrant Officer Senior Service Education (WOSSE).
   g. Duties.
        (1) WO1/CW2. As a Target Acquisition Platoon Leader, Field Artillery Intelligence Officer
and/or Targeting officer:
              (a) Plans, organizes, implements, monitors, and evaluates operations, threat
environment, and unit maintenance of field artillery radar systems.
              (b) Provides advice on technical and tactical employment of field artillery radar
systems.
              (c) Instructs personnel on radar operations and tactical employment of radar
systems.
              (d) Performs reconnaissance and selection of site for emplacement of the radar.
              (e) Assists the S2 and the brigade FSO by performing target value analysis duties.
               (f) Assists in formulating attack guidance used in the brigade and Direct Support (DS)
battalion Command Post (CP) and recommends changes to attack guidance.
              (g) Advise the brigade S2 regarding specific requirements for target location accuracy
and the duration that targets may be considered viable for attack.
              (h) Assists in producing target selection standards for the brigade.
              (i) Serve as assistant counter fire officer.
              (j) Develops pattern analysis of enemy artillery for deliberate targeting purposes.
              (k) Assists the Brigade Combat Team (BCT) S-2 is tying the weapons location radars
to the information collection plan (ICP).
              (l) Serves as the fires representative in the BCT S-2 section to conduct reverse IPB
during mission analysis.
        (2) CW3.As a Field Artillery Intelligence Officer and Targeting Officer:
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (1).
              (b) Evaluates the technical and tactical operations of field artillery radar sections.
              (c) Recommends target purging criteria to the S3 at Field Artillery Brigade (FAB) and
Division Artillery (DIVARTY) level.
              (d) Monitors the processing of target requests and reviews battle damage
assessment at FAB and DIVARTY level.
              (e) Recommends the employment and directs the operation of available TA assets at
FAB and DIVARTY level.
              (f) Monitors the development of the enemy artillery order of battle (OB) and the
processing of target information and intelligence generated by the OB section at FAB and DIV
level.
              (g) Assists in production and application of target selection standards.
              (h) Requests targeting information from military intelligence and higher sources and
evaluates information obtained through the IPB process.
              (i) Selects and expedites critical target information to the fire support systems.
              (j) Develops a targeting process conducive with BCT operations.
              (k) Assist the BCT FSO in production and application of attack guidance matrix,
target selection standards, high-payoff target list and target synchronization matrix.
              (l) Assists the DIV/CORPS G-2 with target value/system analysis.
              (m) Contributes to the information collection plan to identify High-Payoff Targets
(HPT) at the DIV/CORPS level.
        (3) CW4. As a Targeting Officer and Field Artillery Intelligence Officer:
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (2).
              (b) Advises the Division CDR and FSCOORD on all matters concerning targeting.
              (c) Assists the DIV/CORPS G-2 in developing an ICP based on targeting priorities.
              (d) Monitors the development of the enemy artillery OB and the processing of target
information and intelligence generated by the OB section at Division and Corps level.
              (e) Assists in production and application of target selection standards at Division and
Corps level.
              (f) Requests targeting information from military intelligence and higher sources and
evaluates information obtained through the IPB process at Division and Corps level.
        (4) CW5--
              (a) Performs duties described in paragraph g (3).
              (b) Advises the Corps Commander on all matters pertaining to targeting and
employment of all target acquisition assets.
              (c) Performs all targeting duties as described in (3) above at a level appropriate and
necessary for the most senior Targeting Technician in the Corps.
              (d) Advises the Commandant at the Field Artillery School on all matters pertaining to
targeting, and worldwide Targeting Technician personnel status.
              (e) Monitors threat situation, keeps deputy FSCOORD informed, and recommends
changes to priorities and attack means at Corps level.
             (f) Coordinates between the CTOCSE and the Tactical Control and Analysis Element
(TCAE) to ensure potential targets are recognized and passed expeditiously to the fire support
cell.
              (g) Provides detailed information regarding accuracy requirements and how old
information can be before it is no longer of used to the fire support system.
             (h) Ensures attack managers understand how important identification of the target is
and when such identification is critical to the targeting effort.
             (i) Analyzes and recommends changes to commanders targeting and attack
guidance and coordinates target acquisition assets for the Corps.
    h. Physical demands category, grading and position titles.
          (1) Physical Demands Category (PDC) – Moderate.
          (2) Table 8-131A-1. Physical requirements.
          (3) Authorized position titles are provided in tables 6-2 and 6-3. The following grades
are used to code positions into one of four definable skill levels. W2 equals WO1/CW2; W3
equals CW3; W4 equals CW4; and W5 equals CW5. The grades are listed in the following
standards of grade tables:
             (a) Table 8-131A-2. Standards of grade TOE/MTOE.
             (b) Table 8-131A-3. Standards of grade TDA.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
